To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fraction of disorder in reconstituted myoglobins is minimized if the protein is reconstituted in the presence of a high-spin haem derivative within an experimentally defined optimum pH range of approximately 8-9.
the disordered component of myoglobin can be reduced to very low levels if reconstitution is carried by the method described in the text.
the fraction of haem disorder in reconstituted myoglobin depends on the type of haem derivative used in the reconstitution and on the pH of the solution in which the reconstitution is performed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the haem disorder in myoglobin.
the study of the haem disorder in modified apomyoglobins.
the study of the structure and function of myoglobin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fraction of the disordered component is a function of the reconstitution procedure used, and is not a function of the nature of the apoprotein, the nature of the haem, the pH, or the presence of ligands.
the disordered component is not due to the reconstitution procedures used, and that the presence of this component is an intrinsic property of myoglobin.
the fraction of the disordered haem component is minimized when the reconstitution is performed with ferric haem under the optimum conditions described.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reconstitution procedures used here, which are similar to those used in the reconstitution of myoglobin from apomyoglobin, do not produce a fully functional haemoprotein, and that the reconstitution of apomyoglobin with haem derivatives is not a simple process.

reconstitution with low-spin ferric or ferrous derivatives results in a high fraction of disordered haem group and that the fraction of the disordered haem component is minimized by the use of high-spin ferric derivatives.

reconstitution of apomyoglobin with deuterohaemin in the high-spin ferric state within the optimum pH range of pH 8-9 leads to the formation of a myoglobin derivative with a low fraction of disordered haem component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disordered haem group is not a consequence of a particular reconstitution procedure, but is an intrinsic property of the modified myoglobin.
the fraction of haem disorder in reconstituted myoglobins is highly dependent on the reconstitution conditions and is not necessarily a reflection of the quality of the haem derivative used.
the fraction of the disordered component can be minimized by using high-spin ferric derivatives in the optimum pH range of the reconstitution procedure.
